audit.whatIsWrong: Content level chart (win[2]=Gragas, win[3]=Skill, win[4]=Skill) contradicts the packet chart (Skill, Gragas, Gragas) and contradicts its own whys text.
audit.why: whys[2] says level 3 is 'even at best' (Swain gets Nevermove + W bomb), whys[3] says 'you win the extended trades' at 4-5, whys[4] calls level 6 'a genuine all-in'. The packet chart already agrees with the prose; only the enum tokens are stale. Full-layer phases[2..4].side carry the same error.
audit.corrected: win[2]=Skill, win[3]=Gragas, win[4]=Gragas; phases[2].side=Skill, phases[3].side=Gragas, phases[4].side=Gragas. Lane is favoured Gragas (57.42% over 256 games) with a level-3 dip.

audit.why: Spikes are accurate: Gragas at 2 (Q+W), 6 (E-W-Q into Explosive Cask), Riftmaker; Swain at 6 with banked Soul Fragments and on first item. Swain's Ravenous Flock is percent-health-scaling permanent max-HP growth, so his spike curve genuinely climbs with fragments rather than jumping.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page describes Nevermove (E) as 'a short-range root, not a pull, so it only catches you if you walk into him through the wave'. Both halves are wrong.
audit.why: Riot's own text: Swain launches a wave of demonic power forward, it then RETURNS to Swain and roots enemies it hits, and Swain can then choose to pull all rooted champions closer. Range is 850 — longer than your Body Slam (600) and only 50 shorter than Gragas Q's 850. The root lands on the return path, and it is a pull. Advising the player to respect the outgoing throw teaches them to sidestep the wrong half of the ability.
audit.corrected: 850-range projectile; the root triggers on the return leg, then Swain can pull you in. Sidestep the return, not the throw. Cooldown 12/11.5/11/10.5/10 and shorter during Demonic Ascension.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'a whiffed E is 13 seconds of being a barrel with no plan' and 'Swain Demonic Ascension: matchup-defining' with no number.
audit.why: Body Slam is 14/13.5/13/12.5/12 — 14s at rank 1, which is when players actually whiff it. Demonic Ascension is a flat 120s at every rank, which is the single most useful number in this matchup because it never shortens.
audit.corrected: E = 14s at rank 1; Demonic Ascension = flat 120s all ranks; Nevermove = 12s at rank 1.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing on the page tells the player the root is on the return leg or that it converts into a pull.
audit.why: This is the decisive mechanical interaction of the lane — Gragas has no dash out of it once rooted, and the pull drags him back into Death's Hand's stacking bolts.
audit.corrected: Added to early, spikes[3].text and wants.foe[0].

edits.before: Swain's early kill setup hinges on Nevermove (E) — a short-range root, not a pull, so it only catches you if you walk into him through the wave. Hold the line outside E range and his Q (Death's Hand) poke alone can't out-damage your Drunken Rage damage reduction plus Happy Hour healing. At level 2 take Q+W and trade with a drink-empowered auto and a Barrel Roll; he has no W bomb and no root up yet, so you win the short exchange clean.
edits.after: Swain's early kill setup hinges on Nevermove (E) — an 850-range wave that roots on the way BACK, and he can then pull you in, so sidestep the return leg, not the throw. Outside that, his Q (Death's Hand) poke alone can't out-damage your Drunken Rage damage reduction plus Happy Hour healing. At level 2 take Q+W and trade with a drink-empowered auto and a Barrel Roll; he has no W bomb and no root up yet, so you win the short exchange clean.

notes: Both packet suspectNames are FALSE POSITIVES — 'Drunken Rage' and 'Demonic Ascension' are the real Riot names; no ability-name fabrication in this matchup. Level chart in the content layer was inverted against the packet AND against its own whys prose; proposed as one atomic group together with the full-layer phases sides. Not asserted (not in Riot text): whether Nevermove's root is cleansable/QSS-able, whether Explosive Cask's knockback interrupts the Demonic Ascension drain tether, and whether Gragas Body Slam can be Flash-buffered mid-charge — all left alone per the empty-needsResearch rule.
